ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(robotwin): generate 100 instruction candidates per reset, seeded …
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(robotwin): generate 100 instruction candidates per reset, seeded by the episode (#5355)

RoboTwinEnv.reset() builds the official block-ranking instruction by calling
RoboTwin's generate_episode_descriptions() with max_descriptions=1,000,000,
then keeps a single sentence. The block-ranking templates have no
object-description placeholders, so each template fills to one fixed
sentence and the candidate lists only repeat a small, fixed set of
sentences in each split. Building them dominated reset time.

- Default LEROBOT_ROBOTWIN_INSTRUCTION_MAX to 100, as RoboTwin's own
  collect/eval scripts do. The set of distinct candidates is unchanged.
  Non-integer or non-positive values now raise ValueError.
- Pass the episode seed to the generator when it accepts `seed`
  (RoboTwin >= 724b05e), and pick with random.Random(f"{seed}:select")
  instead of np.random.choice, matching eval_policy_xpolicylab.py. With
  such RoboTwin versions the instruction depends only on the seed and
  scene; older versions stay callable, but their candidate order still
  depends on the global Python RNG. The final pick no longer advances the
  global NumPy RNG.

The sentence picked for a given seed changes.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(yam): controller lifecycle fixes and feedback freshness from moto…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(yam): controller lifecycle fixes and feedback freshness from motorbridge 0.6 (#5380)

* fix(yam): leave torque off when the controller fails to start

Enable torque inside the guarded block, and disable it if enabling or starting the
control thread fails, including motors a failed enable_all already turned on.

* fix(yam): raise torque-off failures and still close CAN

disable_torque no longer swallows errors: stop() and disconnect() report them, while
CAN and the cameras are still closed so the motors' CAN timeout stops the arm. A failed
connection cleans up without masking the original error.

* fix(yam): stop arms independently and share only faults between them

Stopping one arm's controller set the stop event both arms share, so recalibrating one
arm of a BiYamFollower silently ended the other arm's loop and let it drop after the CAN
timeout. Each controller now has its own stop signal; the shared event, renamed
fault_event, is only set by faults, which still stop both arms. start() refuses to run
after a fault until the owner clears the event on connect.

* fix(yam): compute gravity torques outside the controller lock

The gravity model can take a while; computing it under the lock blocked latest() and
set_target() callers for that time.

* fix(yam): name controllers after the robot, not its id

str(self.id) gave "None" for robots without an id; str(self) names the robot and its
id in thread names and error messages.

* fix(yam): require placo up front when gravity compensation is on

Check it when the robot is built, with the yam extra install hint, instead of failing
later while loading the gravity model.

* refactor(yam): download the gravity model from the robot-urdfs dataset

Load yam/v1/linear_4310.urdf from the lerobot/robot-urdfs dataset with hf_hub_download
instead of the bucket, and remove ensure_bucket_file and the bucket constants, which only
YAM used.

* test(yam): cover the controller fixes and slim the YAM tests

Add regression tests for the fixes: torque stays off after a failed start, torque-off
failures raise after closing CAN, stopping one arm leaves the other running while a fault
stops both, and recalibrating one arm keeps the other under control. Share the YAM mocks
in tests/mocks/mock_yam.py, and merge or remove overlapping tests.

* refactor(yam): check feedback freshness with motorbridge 0.6 snapshots and drop python-can

* doc(yam): add mit cmd equation

* refactor(yam): move the robot-urdfs repo id to lerobot.utils.constants

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(praxis): backward numerics, padded-chunk frame stacks, merged dev…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(praxis): backward numerics, padded-chunk frame stacks, merged device, raw bimanual gripper (#5328)

Four fixes to the Praxis-1 policy from a review of #5321, each with a test that fails on main.

- Training backward under the praxis numerics. `forward` pins float32 matmuls without TF32 (the
  MoE router scores in float32), but the backward ran later under the host's flags, and
  `lerobot-train` turns TF32 on by default: the router's float32 backward GEMMs and the
  activation-checkpoint recompute of each block (which recomputes the router logits, so a
  near-tied expert choice can flip, silently, since the dispatch keeps its shapes) ran in TF32.
  A hook on the loss now runs the whole backward under the same guard and restores the host
  flags at its end. The gradients no longer depend on `--tf32`.
- Frame stacks after a padded chunk. The first chunk of a context window has 21 real commands,
  padded to 24 with the last one. A caller that executed all 24 rows and handed over the 24
  frames shifted the next chunk's context by 3 frames (the session reads the last 21 executed
  frames). The frames of the padded rows are now dropped, so the next chunk is the one of a
  caller that executed the 21 real commands.
- The merge tool keeps the base config's device. It loads the base on `--device` (default
  `cpu`) and saved that device into the merged checkpoint, so loading it later without
  `--policy.device` put the 27B model on the CPU.
- The bimanual proprio keeps the raw gripper value, as its training data and the praxis
  session do; the single-arm rig keeps clipping it to [0, 1] like the DROID data code. A YAM
  reading slightly outside [0, 1] gave different commands from the praxis session.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: docs(praxis): refresh stale statements; no internal path in the base …
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
docs(praxis): refresh stale statements; no internal path in the base fixture (#5325)

* docs(praxis): the public checkpoint names, the LeRobot 0.7 lock, praxis-sim on PyPI

- The checkpoints are named by their public Hub repositories throughout the guide, the model card
  README, the examples README, code comments and test docstrings: `runwayml/praxis-1-droid-lerobot`
  is the released single-arm DROID checkpoint (54 GB, sharded), `runwayml/praxis-1-yam-lerobot` the
  bimanual checkpoint for two YAM arms, `runwayml/praxis-1-base-lerobot` the backbone and
  action-expert trunk without the heads of a rig. The earlier, unreleased DROID checkpoint of the
  results section is called that. Labels of training runs and export directories are gone.
- The page said LeRobot 0.7.0 locks transformers 5.22.1; main is LeRobot 0.7.1 and locks 5.22.2,
  which gives the same commands as 5.22.1 (checked on the DROID and the YAM checkpoint against the
  praxis repository), so the installation paragraph, the warning, the results and the parity notes
  name the 0.7 lock and both patch versions.
- `praxis-sim` is on PyPI (0.1.0, the code of the praxis repository's `packages/praxis-sim`): the
  vendoring note says so and the resources table gets a Simulator row. LeRobot has no environment
  for it yet.
- References to a private repository's pull requests and commits are replaced by the public
  praxis-1-oss `main` and the vendored commit the file headers name.
- `examples/praxis/README.md` lists `compute_norm_stats.py` and `init_heads.py` (the base
  checkpoint) and notes the converter's own `SHA256SUMS` and the base checkpoint's missing
  processors.

No code change: comments and docstrings only in the Python files.

* test(praxis): the base fixture's provenance names the public checkpoint

The base checkpoint fixture carried the provenance block of its training run, with a storage path
and a codename. The block now names the public Hub repository of the weights,
`runwayml/praxis-1-base-lerobot`, as the public config does, and describes the checkpoint in plain
words. Nothing reads the values: the config check only allows the key, and the base-checkpoint test
skips the block.
